minors.name: Chemical Engineering
minors.school: School of Engineering
minors.philosophy: The Minor in Chemical Engineering gives students from other engineering and science disciplines a working foundation in the principles that govern process industries. Its six courses cover transport phenomena, reaction systems and process design fundamentals — together, the intellectual backbone of the discipline. The aim is to complement a student's parent discipline with quantitative tools that transfer directly to energy systems, environmental technology, materials processing, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals and sustainable manufacturing.
why: Strong analytical and process engineering foundation — rigorous quantitative skills in mass, energy, transport and reaction systems.
Interdisciplinary advantage — the ability to bridge a parent discipline with chemical process knowledge and work on integrated, large-scale systems.

Career and higher-study prospects — pathways into petrochemicals, agrochemicals, bioenergy, bulk and speciality chemicals, sustainability sectors and R&D, and a stronger application for postgraduate study.
glance: Students from other engineering and science disciplines
Six core courses, all of which must be completed
notes: All six courses are required.

minors.name: Civil Engineering
minors.school: School of Engineering
minors.philosophy: The Minor in Civil Engineering opens the built-environment disciplines — surveying, materials, geotechnics, transportation, water and environment — to students from other programs. Three pathways are defined so that the course load suits the student's own major and prior preparation. Each pathway pairs a short compulsory core with a wider optional basket.
why: Foundational skills in surveying, concrete technology and building information modelling that are used on every construction and infrastructure project.
Interdisciplinary advantage for mechanical, chemical, computing and non-engineering students who work at the interface of infrastructure, planning and environment.
Career and higher-study prospects in infrastructure, construction, water resources, transportation and environmental consultancy.
glance: 18 minimum (Mechanical/Chemical and CSE/ECE pathways); 19 minimum (non-SoE pathway)

minors.name: Computer Science & Engineering
minors.school: School of Engineering
minors.philosophy: Undergraduate students who are not majoring in Computer Science & Engineering may take a Minor in CSE. The program builds from data structures through systems, algorithms, databases and artificial intelligence, so that a student acquires the computational vocabulary now expected across every discipline. Two pathways are defined — one for engineering and non-engineering majors generally, and one for students majoring in Electrical and Computer Engineering.
why: Foundational skills in programming, data structures and algorithmic thinking that underpin all computational work.
Interdisciplinary advantage in applying computing to problems in the student's own discipline, from simulation to data analysis.
Career and higher-study prospects across software, data and technology roles, and a credible base for postgraduate study in computing.

minors.name: Electrical and Computer Engineering
minors.school: School of Engineering
minors.department: Department of Electrical Engineering / Electrical and Computer Engineering
minors.philosophy: The Minor in Electrical and Computer Engineering covers signals, digital and analogue electronics, electromagnetics, control, machines and power systems, with electives reaching into sensors, nanoelectronics, communication and energy systems. Four separate baskets are defined so that entry requirements and course selection match the student's own major. A student earns the minor by completing a minimum of 20 credits from the basket applicable to them.
why: Foundational skills in circuits, signals and systems that sit underneath most modern hardware and instrumentation.
Interdisciplinary advantage in embedded systems, robotics, instrumentation and energy — fields where electrical knowledge is the limiting factor for students from other disciplines.
Career and higher-study prospects in electronics, communications, power, semiconductors and control, and a base for postgraduate study in the area.
glance: 20 minimum, earned from the basket applicable to the student's major

minors.name: Mechanical Engineering
minors.school: School of Engineering
minors.philosophy: Students from other departments may take a minor in the Mechanical stream. Four mandatory courses establish manufacturing, drawing, mechanics and thermodynamics, and an optional basket then extends into solids, fluids, heat transfer, design and industrial engineering. The structure is deliberately broad so that students can steer the minor towards either the thermal-fluids or the design-and-manufacturing side of the discipline.
why: Foundational skills in engineering mechanics, thermodynamics and manufacturing processes that apply to any physical product or system.
Interdisciplinary advantage for students in computing, electrical, chemical and science programs who work on hardware, robotics, energy or manufacturing.
Career and higher-study prospects in manufacturing, automotive, energy, aerospace and industrial engineering.

minors.name: Archaeology
minors.school: School of Humanities and Social Sciences
minors.philosophy: The Department of History offers a separate Minor in Archaeology. Its purpose is to enable students to interpret and use material evidence, to learn field methods specific to archaeology, and to understand how archaeological material is treated after excavation through analysis, curation and display. Students are also introduced to the theoretical debates that shape the discipline.
why: Foundational skills in reading material evidence and in the field methods, recording and analysis particular to archaeology.
Interdisciplinary advantage in combining material and textual evidence, which sharpens historical, anthropological and heritage work alike.
Career and higher-study prospects through specialised postgraduate programs in Archaeology and in Museum Studies.

minors.name: History
minors.school: School of Humanities and Social Sciences
minors.philosophy: The Department of History offers an Undergraduate Minor in History to students majoring in other disciplines, through courses offered as University-Wide Electives each semester. The minor is intended for students who want a deeper methodological understanding of the discipline and the chance to explore its core issues, thematic range and analytical approaches. Students choose across core courses and departmental electives.
why: Foundational skills in handling evidence, reading critically and constructing an argument from contested sources.
Interdisciplinary advantage in situating any field: science, engineering, management or the arts, within the longer history that shaped it.
Career and higher-study prospects in research, law, policy, journalism, publishing, heritage and the civil services.

minors.name: History and Archaeology (Combined)
minors.school: School of Humanities and Social Sciences
minors.philosophy: Archaeology and History represent two distinct but interrelated approaches to analysing the past, and this combined minor is built on that relationship. It is offered to students majoring in other disciplines through courses available as University-Wide Electives each semester. Students must draw equally from both streams, so that material and textual evidence are learned alongside one another.
why: Foundational skills in both documentary and material evidence, and in the distinct methods each demands.
Interdisciplinary advantage from working across two allied disciplines rather than one, which broadens the range of questions a student can ask of the past.
Career and higher-study prospects in historical and archaeological research, heritage management, museums, policy and the civil services.

minors.name: Visual Arts
minors.school: School of Humanities and Social Sciences
minors.department: Department of Art, Media and Performance
minors.philosophy: The Minor in Visual Arts combines the history and theory of images with sustained studio practice. Students work across drawing, painting, collage, digital media, photography and the moving image, while building the critical vocabulary to read images and objects. Practice and interpretation are taught together rather than in sequence.
why: Foundational skills in visual thinking, making and critical interpretation of images and objects.
Interdisciplinary advantage for students in design, communication, humanities and technology, where visual literacy increasingly determines how well work is understood.
Career and higher-study prospects in art practice, curation, publishing, media production and postgraduate study in art history or visual culture.
glance: Six courses of 4 credits are on offer; any five complete the minor

minors.name: Dance
minors.school: School of Humanities and Social Sciences
minors.department: Department of Art, Media and Performance
minors.philosophy: The Minor in Dance treats movement as both an embodied practice and an object of critical study. Studio training in technique, alignment and composition runs alongside courses on dance history, aesthetics, and the politics of the body. Students may also move into pedagogy and the use of digital media in performance.
why: Foundational skills in movement technique, anatomy and choreographic composition, together with the vocabulary of performance analysis.
Interdisciplinary advantage in linking embodied practice to questions of identity, gender, power and nationalism drawn from the wider humanities.
Career and higher-study prospects in performance, choreography, dance education, arts management, and postgraduate study in performance studies.
glance: Ten courses of 4 credits are on offer; any six complete the minor

minors.name: Communication
minors.school: School of Humanities and Social Sciences
minors.department: Department of Art, Media and Performance
minors.philosophy: The Minor in Communication is built around film and the moving image, taught as both craft and critical practice. Production courses in image, sound, editing and post-production sit alongside courses in film history and interpretation. Students may extend the minor towards interactive art, photography and environmental communication.
why: Foundational skills in film and television production, editing, sound and image-making.
Interdisciplinary advantage in communicating complex material to real audiences — useful in any discipline, and essential in media, policy and the environmental sciences.
Career and higher-study prospects in film and television, digital media, journalism, advertising and postgraduate study in media and film studies.

minors.name: Design
minors.school: School of Humanities and Social Sciences
minors.philosophy: Design is an applied art and science that involves examining existing situations critically, identifying and redefining problems, exploring solutions laterally, and arriving at innovative and sustainable answers to real user needs. It draws on art, craft, architecture, engineering and the social sciences, and is now recognised as a transdisciplinary field capable of addressing complex twenty-first-century problems. The minor offers experiential learning in multidisciplinary groups, with two tracks — Product Design and Visual Communication.
why: Exposure to design as a field of study, equipping students for further study or competitive examinations in design.
Transdisciplinary skills through collaboration in multidisciplinary groups, breaking down disciplinary boundaries.
A Design Thinking approach — a human-centred method emphasising empathy, ideation, prototyping and iteration, applicable within any discipline.
goals: Students will develop a foundational understanding of design as a field of study and its relevance in contemporary society and industry.
Students will acquire knowledge and application skills of visual language, enabling effective communication across diverse design domains.
Students will understand the human-centred nature of design and gain familiarity with key design methods, processes and techniques.
Students will develop practical skills in creative problem-solving through collaborative, multidisciplinary teamwork.

minors.name: Economics
minors.school: School of Humanities and Social Sciences
minors.philosophy: The Minor in Economics gives students a working command of microeconomic and macroeconomic reasoning and the quantitative methods that support it. The sequence moves from the principles courses into intermediate microeconomics, with econometrics available for students who want empirical training. Requirements are set so that the minor adds genuinely new coursework rather than duplicating a student's major.
why: Foundational skills in economic reasoning, optimisation and the interpretation of empirical evidence.
Interdisciplinary advantage in any field where incentives, markets, policy or data play a role — engineering, management, public policy and the sciences alike.
Career and higher-study prospects in finance, consulting, analytics, research and public policy, and a base for postgraduate study in economics.
glance: All students in good academic standing; there are no other entry requirements

minors.name: English
minors.school: School of Humanities and Social Sciences
minors.philosophy: Students from disciplines other than English may earn a Minor in English. Requirements differ by batch: students admitted before 2025 complete a broader set of departmental courses, while those admitted from 2025 onwards follow a defined core-and-elective structure. The courses range across language, Renaissance drama, linguistics, creative writing and the novel.
why: Foundational skills in close reading, argument and clear writing — the most portable skills a degree can offer.
Interdisciplinary advantage in interpreting texts, framing arguments and understanding how language constructs meaning, whatever the primary discipline.
Career and higher-study prospects in publishing, communications, law, education, the creative industries and postgraduate study in literature.
glance: Students of the University from disciplines other than English

minors.name: International Relations
minors.school: School of Humanities and Social Sciences
minors.department: Department of International Relations and Governance Studies
minors.philosophy: The Minor in International Relations introduces students to the study of states, institutions and the international system, and to the theoretical traditions through which that system is interpreted. Two mandatory core courses establish the field, and students then choose from the Department's major elective basket. The minor suits students who want to situate their own discipline within a global political frame.
why: Foundational skills in the concepts and theoretical traditions used to analyse international politics.
Interdisciplinary advantage in reading global political and institutional context, which bears on technology policy, trade, energy, environment and business strategy.
Career and higher-study prospects in diplomacy, the civil services, international organisations, policy research, journalism and postgraduate study in international relations.
glance: Two mandatory core courses plus any four courses from the Department's major elective basket

minors.name: Sociology
minors.school: School of Humanities and Social Sciences
minors.philosophy: The Minor in Sociology introduces students to the systematic study of social life: institutions, inequality, culture and social change, and to the methods sociologists use to investigate them. Students complete a combination of core and elective courses offered by the Department.
why: Foundational skills in social theory and in qualitative and quantitative methods of social research.
Interdisciplinary advantage in understanding the social context in which technologies, markets and policies actually operate.
Career and higher-study prospects in research, development and policy work, human resources, journalism and postgraduate study in the social sciences.
glance: Any 3 core courses and 3 elective courses in Sociology

minors.name: Management
minors.school: School of Management and Entrepreneurship
minors.philosophy: The Minor in Management is open to undergraduate students in their third and fourth years, and is built on the School's courses that are offered as University-Wide Electives. Rather than prescribing a fixed sequence, it allows students to accumulate 18 credits across operations, analytics, marketing, organisational behaviour, finance, strategy and sustainability. A minimum GPA must be maintained across all School of Management and Entrepreneurship courses taken.
why: Foundational skills in management thinking across analytics, marketing, finance and organisational behaviour.
Interdisciplinary advantage for engineering, science and humanities students who will lead teams, launch ventures or work at the interface of technology and business.
Career and higher-study prospects in consulting, product management, analytics, finance and entrepreneurship, and a base for postgraduate management study.

minors.name: Biotechnology
minors.school: School of Natural Sciences
minors.philosophy: The Department of Life Sciences offers a Minor in Biotechnology to students pursuing majors across the University. Four compulsory courses establish cell biology, microbiology, biochemistry and molecular biology, and students then choose optional courses from the B.Sc. (Research) Biotechnology curriculum. Entry is limited and competitive.
why: Foundational skills in the molecular and cellular basis of life, and in the laboratory reasoning that supports biological research.
Interdisciplinary advantage at the interfaces where much current work sits — bioinformatics, biomedical devices, bioprocess engineering and environmental biotechnology.
Career and higher-study prospects in biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, healthcare and research, and a base for postgraduate study in the life sciences.
glance: 21 credits minimum (12 compulsory + at least 9 optional)

minors.name: Chemistry
minors.school: School of Natural Sciences
minors.philosophy: Undergraduate students who are not majoring in Chemistry may take a Minor in Chemistry. The structure moves in three stages: an introductory category covering chemical principles, equilibrium and physical methods; a foundation category spanning organic, inorganic and physical chemistry; and a single in-depth elective chosen freely from the Department's catalogue. It is the most credit-intensive of the science minors.
why: Foundational skills in chemical principles, structure, bonding, reactivity and the instrumental methods used to study them.
Interdisciplinary advantage in materials, energy, environment and the life sciences, where chemical understanding is often the limiting factor.
Career and higher-study prospects in chemical, pharmaceutical and materials industries, and a base for postgraduate study in chemistry and allied fields.
glance: 27 credits = 24 compulsory (12 Introductory, Category A + 12 Foundation, Category B) + 3 in-depth elective (Category C)

minors.name: Mathematics
minors.school: School of Natural Sciences
minors.philosophy: Undergraduate students who are not majoring in Mathematics may take a Minor in Mathematics. Beyond the pleasure of the subject itself, the minor serves two distinct purposes: acquiring the academic background for higher studies in mathematics, and acquiring the modelling and computational skills needed to apply mathematics in other disciplines or in industry. Credits are earned as University-Wide Electives from courses offered by the Department.
why: Foundational skills in analysis, algebra, probability and numerical methods, and in rigorous proof.
Interdisciplinary advantage in modelling and computation — the shared language of the sciences, engineering, economics and data-driven work.
Career and higher-study prospects in analytics, quantitative finance, computing and research, and a base for postgraduate study in mathematics.
glance: 20 credits minimum, taken as University-Wide Electives from courses offered by the Department of Mathematics

minors.name: Physics
minors.school: School of Natural Sciences
minors.philosophy: A Minor in Physics has two aspects: it ensures a student is well versed in the central core of physics, and it allows the student to pursue more advanced aspects of the subject according to their own interests. The minor equips students to engage with challenging multi-disciplinary problems. It is equally valuable for students seeking employment in industry or in finance, where the physicist's skill in building quantitative models of complex situations is welcomed.
why: Foundational skills in mechanics, thermal physics, quantum mechanics and experimental method.
Interdisciplinary advantage in quantitative modelling of complex systems, which transfers to engineering, computation, the life sciences and finance.
Career and higher-study prospects in research, technology and quantitative finance, and a base for postgraduate study in physics.
glance: 22 credits minimum for an Engineering major; 28 credits minimum for a Non-Engineering major
